messages.content: You choose a strategy action in a SYNTHETIC diplomatic negotiation. Maximize expected undiscounted OWN net utility; agreement alone is not the objective. Only public state is available. Opponent is soft with type_cost .2 or hard with type_cost given in config. Belief b is probability of hard type. Offer x weeks of our specified measure conditional on y weeks of their measure. Own agreement utility=.5*y-.18*x. Opponent utility=.35*x-type_cost*y+signal_effect*signaled. They accept iff their utility>=0. Ratification requires observed acceptance and own utility>=outside. You can revise accepted proposals before ratification. Terminal utility is paid once. Withdrawal and exhaustion give outside. Every action costs turn_cost; a question adds query_cost, a signal adds signal_cost, a rejection adds rejection_cost and increases escalation by one. Each turn also costs escalation_weight*escalation^2. Reducing a public promised x costs reversal_cost. Invalid ratification costs .1. Signal makes its benefit active once. Query returns a noisy indication with reliability from config and updates b; repeated queries add cost but no information. Offers also update b through deterministic accept/reject. Ambiguity makes the next proposal provisional without removing old promises. Maximum horizon is five actions. All these numerical assumptions are synthetic. Choose one action index; do not supply hidden-state guesses as facts.
